description: P5.6 Conversation history / session management (Section 8.5) AND P5.7 App shell + navigation + least-privilege capabilities + README status flip. The history surface is the natural entry point that resumes a session (restoring persona, route pin, tags, enabled tools), and the app shell assembles all five surfaces and wires the single top-level CoreEvent subscription that fans events into the stores. Lands last because it depends on all prior surfaces being present. Depends on FEAT-001/002/003.
steps: HISTORY (src/features/history/): ConversationList (sorted/filtered index from state/conversations.ts: id, title, timestamps, tags, last route), SearchBar (client-side filter over title/tags), ConversationContextMenu (rename -> renameConversation; tag -> setConversationTags; duplicate -> createConversation seeded from the source's persona/pref/tags, or a dedicated command if FEAT-001 added one, else client-side re-create; export -> exportConversation(id, format) then trigger a download/save of the returned string; delete -> deleteConversation), SessionSummary (model usage/cost/tags derived from message usage + route metadata), NewConversationButton (createConversation).

HISTORY wiring: consume conversation_created / conversation_updated / conversation_deleted via the conversations store (invalidate + refresh the index). Resuming a session: openConversation(id) loads the full conversation; set it active and restore persona (assign already persisted), route pin (conversationPref), privacy tags, and enabledToolServers into the active-conversation state so the chat + model-selector + tool surfaces reflect the resumed session (Section 8.5).

APP SHELL (src/app.tsx + any layout components in src/components/): assemble the five surfaces into a navigable layout (e.g. a sidebar with History + a main pane hosting Chat with the Model selector in/near the Composer, and routes/tabs or panels for Tool manager and Agent editor). Establish ONE top-level onCoreEvent subscription (in a useEffect with a stable cleanup returning the UnlistenFn) that dispatches each CoreEvent to the relevant store's event-application function (fan-out), so surfaces stay in sync without each subscribing independently. Keep the existing app_version display or fold it into an about/status area if desired (do not break app.test.tsx, or update it to match).

CAPABILITIES (P5.7, crates/tauri-app/capabilities/default.json): update the description/comment to enumerate the full Phase 5 command set now exposed and reaffirm least privilege (Section 9.2). In Tauri v2, user #[tauri::command] handlers are authorized by generate_handler! registration, not by capability permission tokens, so keep permissions to `core:default` (no fs/shell/network granted to the webview) unless a specific built-in plugin is genuinely needed — if none is, do NOT add plugin permissions. Ensure the file stays valid JSON and consistent with the registered commands.

README: flip the Phase 5 line in the 'Implementation status' section (README.md line ~35) from 'PENDING' to 'DONE' following the existing PR #6 convention/wording used for Phases 0-4 (a 'DONE.' prefix + a short summary of what shipped: the five wired UI surfaces + any new commands/events).

TESTS (vitest + RTL): history — ConversationList renders and filters via SearchBar; context-menu actions call renameConversation/setConversationTags/exportConversation/deleteConversation; NewConversationButton calls createConversation; feed synthetic conversation_created/updated/deleted and assert the index refreshes; resume via openConversation restores persona/pin/tags/tools into active state. app shell — renders the surfaces; the single onCoreEvent subscription dispatches a synthetic event to the right store (assert a store transition); unlisten is called on unmount. Update app.test.tsx if the shell changed the app_version rendering. Mock invoke + listen.

FINAL LOCAL VERIFY: from hybrid-orchestrator/frontend run `NODE_OPTIONS= npx prettier --check .` across the WHOLE frontend and fix any remaining formatting. Self-audit eslint/tsc across all new/changed files. In findings, report EXACTLY which frontend checks ran locally (prettier) vs deferred to CI (eslint/tsc/vitest) and why (node_modules uninstallable offline, npm 403).
acceptance_criteria: History surface lists/searches conversations, offers rename/tag/duplicate/export/delete via a context menu, shows a session summary and a new-conversation button, and updates on conversation_created/updated/deleted.
Resuming a conversation (openConversation) restores persona, route pin, privacy tags, and enabled tool servers into the active session state.
app.tsx assembles all five surfaces into a navigable layout with a SINGLE top-level onCoreEvent subscription that fans events into the stores and cleans up on unmount.
capabilities/default.json remains least-privilege (core:default; no fs/shell/network to the webview) with its description updated for the Phase 5 command set; it is valid JSON.
README 'Implementation status' shows Phase 5 as DONE with a short summary, matching the Phases 0-4 convention.
vitest/RTL tests cover the history surface and the app shell (rendering, mocked-invoke calls, event fan-out, unlisten on unmount).
`NODE_OPTIONS= npx prettier --check .` passes across the whole frontend.
verification: Run `NODE_OPTIONS= npx prettier --check .` from hybrid-orchestrator/frontend; confirm the whole frontend is clean.
Confirm capabilities/default.json is valid JSON and README shows Phase 5 DONE.
Self-audit ESLint/tsc; report the exact local-vs-CI check matrix in findings (prettier local; eslint/tsc/vitest + all cargo per-crate checks on CI).
findings:
IMPLEMENTED (frontend + capabilities JSON + README; no other Rust touched). HISTORY (src/features/history/): SearchBar (controlled client-side query input; owns no store state), NewConversationButton (createConversation -> resumeConversation so the new session opens), ConversationContextMenu (Rename -> renameConversation via window.prompt; Tag -> setConversationTags via prompt, parsing comma-separated 'localOnly'/'confidential'/custom tags into PrivacyTag[]; Duplicate -> duplicateConversation; Export Markdown/JSON -> exportConversation(id, format) then a Blob + <a download> browser download; Delete -> deleteConversation; all actions delegate to the conversations store which owns the IPC), ConversationList (renders the index filtered client-side by title/tags and sorted by updatedAt desc; each row shows title/timestamp/tags/pinned-route and RESUMES via resumeConversation on click; hosts the ConversationContextMenu per row), SessionSummary (distinct models from message RouteMetadata + aggregate totalTokens from TokenUsage + the active conversation's privacy tags), History container (loads the index on mount, owns the search query, assembles the pieces).

RESUME: added resumeConversation(id) to state/conversations.ts using the open_conversation command (returns OpenedConversation { conversation, messages }); it sets activeConversationId + messages AND refreshes the cached Conversation record so the restored persona (personaId), route pin (conversationPref), privacy tags, and enabledToolServers are current for the chat/model-selector/tool surfaces (which all read the active Conversation record). Also added duplicateConversation(id) (client-side seed over create_conversation with the source title '(copy)'/personaId/privacyTags, then carries the route pin via set_conversation_route since create_conversation does not accept it) and exportConversation(id, format) (thin delegate to the export_conversation command) to the store. HISTORY event wiring reuses the existing conversations-store applyCoreEvent (conversationCreated/Updated invalidate+refetch the index, conversationDeleted drops the row) fed by the shell fan-out.

APP SHELL (src/app.tsx): assembled ALL FIVE surfaces into a navigable layout - a left sidebar hosting the History surface, a main pane with a tablist switching Chat (MessageList + RoutingModeToggle model selector + Composer + PermissionPrompt) / Tools (ToolManager) / Agents (AgentEditor), and a StatusBar footer that KEEPS the Phase 0 app_version display (data-testid='app-version'). Established ONE top-level onCoreEvent subscription in a useEffect (empty deps; reads each store's applyCoreEvent via getState() so nothing reactive is closed over) that fans every CoreEvent payload out to all four stores' applyCoreEvent; the cleanup awaits the listen() promise and calls the UnlistenFn exactly once on unmount.

CAPABILITIES (crates/tauri-app/capabilities/default.json): description updated to enumerate the full Phase 5 command surface (conversations/personas/providers/permissions/MCP groups) and reaffirm least privilege - permissions stay ['core:default'] with NO fs/shell/network and NO plugin permissions (Tauri v2 user #[tauri::command] handlers are authorized by generate_handler! registration, not capability tokens). Verified valid JSON (python json.load).

README: flipped the Phase 5 'Implementation status' line from 'PENDING' to a 'DONE.' entry matching the Phases 0-4 convention, summarizing the five wired surfaces + the new commands + the runtime MCP handle manager.

TESTS (vitest + RTL, vi.mock invoke + listen): features/history/history.test.tsx (ConversationList renders sorted + filters by title and by tag; SearchBar filters the History list; NewConversationButton create->resume; context menu Rename/Tag/Delete call the matching commands with camelCase args, Duplicate seeds create_conversation + carries the pin via set_conversation_route, Export downloads the returned string via a stubbed URL.createObjectURL + anchor click; conversation_created/_updated refetch + _deleted drops the row; resume via open_conversation restores persona/pin/tags/enabledToolServers + messages into active state; SessionSummary derives models/tokens/tags). Extended state/conversations.test.ts (resumeConversation, duplicateConversation, exportConversation). Rewrote app.test.tsx for the new shell: still asserts the app_version render, plus asserts the five surfaces render, that exactly ONE listen() subscription is opened and its handler dispatches a synthetic providersChanged event into the providers store (asserts store.load fires), and that unlisten is called on unmount.

LOCAL vs CI CHECK MATRIX. RAN LOCALLY: `NODE_OPTIONS= npx prettier --check .` from hybrid-orchestrator/frontend -> PASSES ('All matched files use Prettier code style!') across the WHOLE frontend (two files were prettier --write'd during development, then the whole tree re-checked clean). DEFERRED TO CI (node_modules uninstallable offline: npm registry returns 403, no node_modules present): eslint (`npm run lint` = eslint .), tsc (`npm run build` = tsc && vite build / tsc --noEmit), and vitest (`npm run test` = vitest run) on ubuntu-latest + windows-latest; ALL cargo per-crate checks (fmt/clippy -D warnings/test) are CI-only (crates.io unreachable offline) - and this feature touched no Rust source, only capabilities/default.json (validated as JSON) so no cargo behavior changed. SELF-AUDIT against eslint.config.js (js.recommended + typescript-eslint recommended + react-hooks recommended): no explicit any (used `unknown` + `as unknown as {...}` casts and a `route is NonNullable<...>` type guard instead of a non-null assertion); no unused imports/locals/params; react-hooks exhaustive-deps satisfied (History [loadConversations]; StatusBar []; the shell fan-out useEffect has empty deps and reads store actions via getState() so no reactive value is omitted); no fallthrough (the conversations-store switch returns in every arm). Against tsconfig.json (strict, noUnusedLocals/Parameters, noFallthroughCasesInSwitch): all new code typechecks by inspection; CreateConversationArgs accepts the duplicate seed shape; all lines <=100 cols and TS unions single-line where they fit.
